checkpoints.description: [1/2] Refuse a split GGUF part (name matching -00001-of-00002.gguf) in the Hugging Face resolver with a Fix that points at the single-file quantization; leave names that merely contain of or digits alone. Failing-first resolver tests; [2/2] npm test, aikit check, ADR-143, UI review, commit (G-001 not applicable: resolver only)

impact_assessment.why: A split part downloads like any GGUF, then the library's spliceSplitFiles:false scan and the loader cannot use it alone, so the user pays a multi-GB download for a model that cannot load
impact_assessment.benefits: The refusal happens before any network request and names the reason; single-file quants keep working
impact_assessment.risks: contract: one more invalid reference (a file that could never load); dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: the pattern requires the five-digit HF split suffix, so ordinary names with of or digits are unaffected; tests cover both sides

Task 'no-split-parts' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Keep the Hugging Face host rule in one exported helper (assertHuggingFaceFileUrl) and call it from inspectSource and startSource too, so a direct caller can never send the token to a non-Hugging-Face first hop or download another host; refuse a non-string SHA-256 instead of ignoring it. Failing-first tests for both methods; [2/2] npm test, a full pinned live import in a temp home (download, header check, promotion, receipt, Installed line), aikit check, ADR-144, UI review, commit (G-001 not applicable: download path only)

impact_assessment.why: Only the route enforced the host; the methods are exported and one direct call would send the HF token on the first request to any host and could download any https file, and a numeric sha256 was silently dropped
impact_assessment.benefits: The guardrail lives in one module and every source entry point enforces it; a mistyped pin is refused instead of unpinning the file
impact_assessment.risks: contract: source methods refuse non-HF URLs and non-string pins; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: the canonical resolver URL and www host still pass; catalog downloads do not use these methods; tests pin both refusals and no engine/job is created

checkpoints.description: [1/2] When /api/models/add-hf answers with an already-complete job (same URL and receipt), the form says Already in your library instead of Download started, marks the job id as seen so the poll does not toast a second time, and keeps the row list empty because complete jobs are not shown. Failing-first ui:smoke fixture path; [2/2] npm test, ui:smoke, aikit check, ADR-146, UI review, commit (G-001 not applicable: UI wording only)

impact_assessment.why: ADR-142 makes re-adding the same URL idempotent, but the UI still announced a download that never ran and then let the poll announce completion for it
impact_assessment.benefits: The user gets one truthful message for an already-installed file and no phantom progress or duplicate toast
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none (same request, same job); dependency: none; concurrency: the poll already keys on job id; state: a seen-id entry in the existing set
impact_assessment.mitigation: the complete branch is keyed on the job status the server returns, not on a guess; the smoke fixture returns a complete job and asserts the message

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Engine ready states report requestedContextSize (the effective request after the 16K floor and before the trained cap) in load and context-rebuild, and idle reports null; the UI clamp note reads it instead of guessing from the saved setting, which can differ under a tuned profile. Failing-first engine test with a 4096-trained fake runtime; [2/2] npm test, ui:smoke, aikit check, ADR-147, UI review, commit (G-001 not applicable: additive status field, no generation change)

impact_assessment.why: ADR-145 compared the served context with the saved setting, but a tuned load can request a different context; the note could name the wrong requested value or hide a clamp
impact_assessment.benefits: The status is self-describing and the note is correct whatever applied the load
impact_assessment.risks: contract: additive status field; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: the field is the same requested value the load already computes; a test pins requested/trained/served on a clamp

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Add tests for the previously untested stdio MCP server: initialize negotiation and fallback, ping, tools/list, notifications, invalid request/method/tool/arguments, forwarding only the allowed tool fields, the passing and failing summaries, ECONNREFUSED, timeout, non-JSON and JSON error replies, and serveStdio's parse-error, notification skip, ordering and internal-error lines. No production change unless a test finds a defect; [2/2] npm test, aikit check, ADR-148, UI review (backend), commit (G-001 not applicable: tests only)

impact_assessment.why: src/mcp-server.js is a public integration surface (Claude Desktop and other MCP clients) with zero tests, so a protocol regression would only appear in a user session
impact_assessment.benefits: The JSON-RPC contract, the tool schema forwarding and every refusal path are pinned by fast unit tests
impact_assessment.risks: contract: tests only; dependency: none; concurrency: serveStdio is deterministic with injected streams; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: fakes for fetch and streams; no network, no model, no spawn; a production change only if a test exposes a real defect, recorded separately
